question.problem:
A smartphone app has $500\,000$ users, $150\,000$ of which have a paid account. If an app developer randomly samples $300$ users, find a normal approximation for the probability that between $72$ and $90$ (inclusive) users in the sample have a paid account. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size. *Hint: Two tables of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.06\,$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$
$\,-2.3\,$ $\,0.0091\,$ $\,0.0089\,$ $\,0.0087\,$
$\,-2.2\,$ $\,0.0119\,$ $\,0.0116\,$ $\,0.0113\,$
$\,-2.1\,$ $\,0.0154\,$ $\,0.0150\,$ $\,0.0146\,$
$z$$\,0.00\,$$\,0.01\,$$\,0.02\,$
$\,-0.1\,$ $\,0.4602\,$ $\,0.4562\,$ $\,0.4522\,$
$\,0.0\,$ $\,0.5000\,$ $\,0.5040\,$ $\,0.5080\,$
$\,0.1\,$ $\,0.5398\,$ $\,0.5438\,$ $\,0.5478\,$
question.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=300,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=\frac{150\,000}{500\,000}=0.3.$

Now, since

$$
np=300(0.3)=90>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=300(1-0.3)=210>5,
$$

and the $n=300$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.3,\frac{0.3(1-0.3)}{300}) \\  & ∼N(0.3,0.0007).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine the probability we wish to find. If between $72$ and $90$ of users in the sample have a paid account, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{72}{300}\le \overset{^}{\,p} & \le \frac{90}{300} \\ 0.24\le \overset{^}{\,p} & \le 0.3.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the probability we wish to find is
$P(0.24\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.3).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.24\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.3) & =P(\frac{0.24-0.3}{\sqrt{0.0007}}\le Z\le \frac{0.3-0.3}{\sqrt{0.0007}}) \\  & ≈P(-2.27\le Z\le 0) \\  & =P(Z\le 0)-P(Z\le -2.27) \\  & =Φ(0)-Φ(-2.27)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0)=0.5000,\,Φ(-2.27)=0.0116.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.24\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.3) & =Φ(0)-Φ(-2.27) \\  & =0.5000-0.0116 \\  & =0.4884.\end{aligned}
$$
